sentences.text: Overoraptor is an extinct genus of paravian theropod with uncertain affinities from the Early Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina. The genus contains one species, O. chimentoi, known from fragmentary bones of the hands, feet, hips, and vertebrae. Overoraptor chimentoi was a gracile theropod measuring approximately 1.3 meters in length, with long arms and legs.
Researchers estimated Overoraptor was about 1.3 meters long, though its mass was not estimated. Gregory S. Paul estimated Overoraptor was about 3 meters long and weighed about 30 kilograms.

Overoraptor possessed a short, robust second toe claw typical of dromaeosaurs. Overoraptor's metacarpals were unusually wide, short, and asymmetrical compared to other non-avian paravians. Overoraptor had a curved ulna, representing the primitive condition for paravians.

The name Overoraptor combines the Spanish word for "piebald" and the Latin word for "thief". The species name chimentoi honors Dr. Roberto Nicolás Chimento, who discovered the remains. The generic name Overoraptor derives from 'overo' because its bones were preserved in a white and black color pattern.
The hind limb showed features very similar to those of running animals, indicating it was very fast.

Fossils were found by Dr. Roberto Nicolás Chimento at the Violante Farm locality in Rio Negro Province, Argentina. Overoraptor was described as a new genus and species in May 2020 by Motta, Agnolín, Brissón Egli, and Novas.
The holotype and paratype specimens were found in a quarry 1.5 meters in diameter and 0.30 meters deep, south of the Ezequiel Ramos Mexía reservoir in Río Negro Province.

The legs possessed a large, curved, and sharp claw on the second toe, similar to unenlagiids. These two species had raptor-type feet and bird-wing-like arms, features absent in Northern Hemisphere unenlagiids and velociraptors.

Anatomical study of the arm bones revealed it shared characteristics with birds that other raptor dinosaurs lacked. These characteristics suggest these two species might belong to a new group of running paravians, phylogenetically closer to birds than to raptors.

Phylogenetic analyses have placed Overoraptor in various positions, but the most supported tree places it as the sister taxon of Rahonavis. Phylogenetic analysis placed Overoraptor and Rahonavis in a novel position, excluding them from the clades Unenlagiidae and Avialae where Rahonavis was previously classified.
Researchers suggest the grouping of Overoraptor with Rahonavis may result from a unique mix of primitive and derived traits in Overoraptor.
The parent group for the genus Overoraptor is Paraves. The genus Overoraptor is classified under the class Reptilia.

Overoraptor lived during the Aptian stage of the Cretaceous period. The dinosaur was found in the Huincul Formation deposits and lived in the Gondwana continental block, now Río Negro Province, Argentina.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for the genus Overoraptor as Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago).
